findings.description: A fork PR opened at the same head SHA as one of the owner's PRs, then retargeted, makes this job write a pending `claude-review` status on that commit. The owner's PR loses its SUCCESS verdict, and getting it back takes a billed `@claude review`.
findings.body:
**Any PR author can now reset the `claude-review` status on someone else's commit.**

A commit status belongs to the repo and the SHA, not to a PR. This job runs under `pull_request_target` with the base repo's token and `statuses: write`. Its only filter is `if: github.event.changes.base`. It writes:

```js
sha: context.payload.pull_request.head.sha,
state: "pending",
context: "claude-review",
```

Before this PR, an outsider could not cause any `claude-review` write: the review job requires `github.actor == github.repository_owner && github.triggering_actor == github.repository_owner` (`claude-code-review.yml` L36-41). Now any GitHub user can:

1. push the head commit of an open owner PR to a fork;
2. open a PR from it;
3. retarget that PR to any other branch (the `feature/*` branches exist).

The job then marks the owner's head `pending: Not reviewed: base branch changed; re-run`. This status is new in this PR, and nothing downstream treats it as finished:

- `pup ci wait` times out and keeps timing out. `reviewDigest` in `src/core/ci-wait.service.ts` L229-270 only accepts SUCCESS, FAILURE, or the comment-only pending text.
- `pup fix` refuses, because it needs a SUCCESS status (ADR 0090).
- `pr-status` labels the PR `pr/ci-pending` on its next recompute.

Recovery is a billed full `@claude review`, and the attacker can retarget again to repeat it. Platform details (fork `pull_request_target` runs without approval, statuses are visible per SHA) come from knowledge, not a spike.

**Fix direction:** reviews only ever run for the owner, so a non-owner PR's `claude-review` status protects nothing. Gate the job on, for example, `github.event.pull_request.user.login == github.repository_owner` or `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`. Then revise the header's "so fork PRs are covered too".

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d79374a06405d318294b1fe4d4b9258b8ed024cb/.github/workflows/claude-review-base-change.yml#L19-L38

findings.description: After a retarget, the next push gets an incremental review of only the push delta (or the preflight skips it as comment-only), so the verdict earned against the old base still satisfies the gate on the new head.
findings.body:
**A push after a retarget restores the gate without reviewing against the new base.**

The header says "The next review (a push, or the owner's `@claude review`) replaces the status". That is true for `@claude review`, which forces `full` mode. It is not true for a push.

The preflight never looks at the base:

- `priorRecords` (`review-preflight.script.ts` L79-106) reads only `commit_sha`, `timestamp`, `is_error` and `partial`.
- `decideMode` measures ancestry and merges from the prior reviewed head only:

```ts
if (!isAncestor || hasMerges) return { kind: "full" };
if (isCommentOnly && trigger !== "comment") return { kind: "skip-comment-only", priorPath: prior.path };
return { kind: "incremental", fromSha: prior.commit_sha, priorPath: prior.path };
```

That leaves two outcomes for a plain push on top of the reviewed head:

- **Incremental review.** It covers only `git diff <prior>..HEAD`. Commits the retarget brought into the PR diff, such as a stacked branch's old base, are ancestors of the prior SHA, so they are never reviewed. The poster still marks the new head reviewed.
- **Comment-only skip.** The preflight posts `Not reviewed: only comments and prose changed since …` on the new head (L204). `pr-status.yml` L133-137 treats that as not running, so with CI green the PR goes straight to `pr/ready`. The base-change marker stays behind on the old SHA.

In both cases, a verdict earned against the old base satisfies the gate, which is what this workflow exists to prevent.

**Fix direction:** have the preflight detect the base change and force `full`. For example, persist the merge base or base ref in the metrics record, and treat a prior record with a different base as no prior. At minimum, correct the header so it does not claim a push restores the gate.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d79374a06405d318294b1fe4d4b9258b8ed024cb/.github/workflows/claude-review-base-change.yml#L1-L3 · https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d79374a06405d318294b1fe4d4b9258b8ed024cb/tools/review/src/preflight.utils.ts#L219-L246

findings.description: The `base branch changed` text is hard-coded in both workflows: `claude-review-base-change.yml:36` writes it, and `pr-status.yml` matches it with `includes(...)` on top of the existing `startsWith("Not reviewed")` prefix. If the description is reworded, `pr-status` silently goes back to treating a retargeted head as not running. Matching one full prefix instead (e.g. `startsWith("Not reviewed: base branch changed")`) keeps a single granularity.

The inline status write nearly duplicates `markNotReviewed` in `tools/review/src/review-preflight.script.ts:63-73` and repeats the `claude-review` context literal a third time. Unlike `markNotReviewed`, which only warns on failure, a `createCommitStatus` error here fails the job. Keep the wording aligned with `markNotReviewed`, or hoist the literals into workflow `env`.

refuted_findings.description: Sharing `claude-review-<PR>` with the review job lets a retarget cancel a review that is queued behind a running one, which silently drops the automatic follow-up review of the latest push.
refuted_findings.refutation: When a retarget cancels a queued review, the job then marks the current head (`context.payload.pull_request.head.sha`) pending with `base branch changed`. This PR's `pr-status.yml` change counts that status as `pr/ci-pending`, so the failure is closed and visible, not silent. The cancelled review would also have run incrementally against the old-base record, which is exactly the verdict the marker exists to block. The reverse ordering ends in the same gate state with or without the shared group, because `decideMode` ignores the base either way (that defect is filed separately under the header finding). The comment's rationale, not racing a review that is posting its verdict, holds.
